description: US-30 Changing a customer's customer number. A customer number is the SLOT a household occupies in DF's register — 1 up to quotaN — and it is the number printed on the card the household carries. Since US-24 staff CHOOSE it at registration from the free ones; after that it is decided for good, and the record says so in as many words („Die Kundennummer lässt sich nicht ändern.“). DF's testing showed that is too rigid: a returning family wants the number their neighbours know them by, a block of numbers is to be kept together, a number was typed in wrongly and noticed a week later. None of those is a fault the software can detect and none needs its opinion. THIS BATCH EXTENDS THE US-24 CHOICE TO A HOUSEHOLD ALREADY ON THE REGISTER: a staff member moves an active or blocked household from the number it holds to any number that is free, from a section on the customer record beside the group control, and A NEW CARD IS ISSUED IN THE SAME ACT so nobody has to remember a second step and nobody can forget one. WORKED: a household on 5 carrying 5k4 moves to 23, whose last card ever printed was 23k5 by a household since archived. Afterwards the household holds 23 and carries 23k6; slot 5 is free and the next registration on it starts at 5k5; the record shows 23k6 and beneath it 5k4, 5k3, 5k2, 5k1 — NONE RE-LABELLED; the household has been issued FIVE cards, not six, because the jump in the index is the SLOT'S history and not theirs. THE INDEX RULE IS NOT NEW: nextCardIndex and CardRepository.highestIndexForNumber already count the slot's whole run including archived holders (US-25), and this batch is simply a fourth caller of it. WHY NO CARD IS EVER RE-LABELLED, and the thing an implementer will get wrong: the four cards left on slot 5 are what makes slot 5 SAFE TO HAND OUT AGAIN — the next household asks the slot for its highest index, gets 4 and is printed 5k5. Re-label them under 23 and slot 5 looks untouched, the next household is printed a 5k1 THAT ALREADY EXISTS out in the world, and the counter answers „Ausgabe frei“ to a dead card. A card is also a real physical object: 5k3 was printed as 5k3, and showing it as 23k3 names a card that either never existed or belongs to somebody else. THE ARCHITECTURAL REVERSAL THIS CARRIES: ADR-007 justifies the stored Card.customerNumber as 'a key the constraint needs' and says it 'snapshots nothing — a customer number is fixed at registration — and is never read as the card's number'. BOTH HALVES STOP BEING TRUE HERE. A card printed on slot 5 keeps 5 while its household moves to 23, so the column becomes a genuine snapshot — the fourth beside grownUpsAtIssue, childrenAtIssue and groupAtIssue — and it MUST be read as the card's number, because the household's own number no longer answers what is printed on an old card. The last story writes ADR-016 and corrects ADR-007, ADR-008, the root CLAUDE.md, schema.prisma, ports.ts, the glossary and the German record hint. NO SCHEMA CHANGE AND NO MIGRATION: Customer.customerNumber is already updatable, Card.customerNumber already exists and is already written per card, and Card.reason is a string the domain validates, so a fifth reason word costs the database nothing. THIS BATCH MUST NOT TOUCH prisma/migrations/. ATOMICITY IS THE POINT: the number change and the card insert are ONE TRANSACTION in one new port method, CustomerRepository.changeCustomerNumber(id, customerNumber, card) — split into setCustomerNumber + issueCard, a crash between them leaves a household on 23 carrying 5k4 and NO QUERY IN THE SYSTEM CAN DETECT IT. The precedent is create(), which already writes a customer and their first card as one. NOTHING IS WRITTEN AT ALL on a refusal — no number change, no card, no audit entry — when the chosen number is taken by an active household, is outside the quota in force, is the one the household already holds, or the household has been archived meanwhile. TWO AUDIT ENTRIES, because two facts happened: { what: 'customer.numberChanged', changedFields: ['customerNumber'], why: 'customerNumber=5→23' } — the numbers ride in why as the one machine-written value the port already documents, exactly as a logged reminder writes 'reminderCount=2' — plus the card's own 'customer.card.issued'. NO REASON IS COLLECTED FROM STAFF: the two numbers are the whole of what happened, and staff's reasons for wanting a particular number are their own (ADR-006). THE INVARIANT THE WHOLE DESIGN RESTS ON: the card a household currently holds is ALWAYS the highest index on the slot they currently hold — registration starts above every predecessor, a reissue counts on from the slot's run, and a number change issues the new card on the new slot in the same transaction as the move. Named tests in read-customer and read-card say so, because nextCardNumber and the counter's OUTDATED_CARD verdict would be quietly wrong if it stopped holding. NO NUMBER HISTORY IS BUILT and the card history reveals one anyway — that is ACCEPTED and deliberate: nothing resolves a household to the numbers it used to hold, no screen asks, but a reader of 5k4 on a household now holding 23 can see they were once on 5, and distorting a correct card history to hide it would be worse. A card number is not a way back either: typing 5k4 at the counter resolves to whoever holds slot 5 TODAY — nobody, or the household that has since taken it — which needs no code, since lookupCustomer already asks the slot through findByCustomerNumber. OUT OF SCOPE: no list or report of previous numbers, no reason or note on the change, no change to allocation at registration or to how card numbers are formed, no moving an archived household, no bulk renumbering and no direct swap of two households' numbers (neither number is free while the other holds it — swap by moving one to a free number first), no limit on how often, no hint at the counter that a number was recently released, and NO UNDO (moving back would consume yet another card number; the confirmation before the write stands in for it).

userStories.title: Which numbers a household may be moved to (domain)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need one pure rule that says which numbers this household may be moved to and whether a chosen one may still be written, so no screen and no use case decides it. Source: tasks/prd-us-30-change-customer-number.md §US-30.1
acceptanceCriteria: In src/domain/customer/customerNumber.ts, BESIDE freeNumbers and assertFreeNumber — the same file, because this is the same question asked from the other end of a household's life. PURE: no I/O, no clock, no import from Next.js, React or Prisma

choosableNumbers(currentNumber, takenNumbers, quotaN): ReadonlyArray<number> — every number in 1..quotaN no ACTIVE household holds, PLUS currentNumber itself, ascending and without duplicates. BUILT ON freeNumbers rather than beside it, so the pool the registration form offers (US-24) and the pool this control offers can never come apart

currentNumber has to be added back because takenNumbers CONTAINS IT — the household is active and holds its own slot. The doc comment says so, since a reader who misses it will 'fix' the duplicate-looking merge

A currentNumber ABOVE quotaN — which a lowered quota (US-14) produces without anybody doing anything wrong — is STILL IN THE LIST and sorts last. The household may keep it and may move down into the quota, but is NEVER FORCED to move

assertChoosableNumber(requested, currentNumber, takenNumbers, quotaN): number returns requested unchanged when it may be written, and otherwise throws IN THIS ORDER: (1) CustomerNumberUnchanged when requested === currentNumber — FIRST, so a household parked above a lowered quota that saves its own number is told it already has that number rather than that the number is out of range; (2) CustomerNumberOutOfRange when requested is not a whole number in 1..quotaN; (3) CustomerNumberTaken when an active household holds it — the SAME error the partial unique index raises, for the reason assertFreeNumber reuses it: it is the same fact found earlier, and the index stays the final authority
Because the unchanged check comes first, the occupancy check needs NO 'except my own number' special case: any requested still in play is somebody else's. The doc comment states that

New CustomerNumberUnchanged in src/domain/errors.ts carrying the number, its code in DomainErrorCode, and tiered 'refusal' in src/app/notice-tier.ts. Modelled on GroupUnchanged and refused for the same reason: a no-op is NOT idempotent here — it would write an audit entry and consume a card number, and a staff member who pressed the button would be told nothing happened

STRICT TDD, invariant-breaking test first, one named test per rule: 'offers every free number and the household's own', 'offers the household's own number first when it is the lowest', 'offers a current number above the quota, last', 'offers only the current number when the register is otherwise full', 'never offers a number another active household holds', 'refuses the number the household already holds', 'refuses the household's own number even when it is above the quota', 'refuses a number outside the quota', 'refuses a number an active household holds', 'accepts a number an archived household once held', 'accepts the lowest free number'

userStories.title: Moving a household to another number (application + ports + infrastructure)
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to move a household to a free number and have the new card issued in the same act, so the record and the card in the household's pocket can never disagree. Source: tasks/prd-us-30-change-customer-number.md §US-30.3 and §US-30.6
acceptanceCriteria: New use case src/application/customers/change-customer-number.ts exporting changeCustomerNumber(deps, { customerId, customerNumber })

It reads the customer, the settings in force (readCurrentSettings — THE QUOTA MAY HAVE BEEN LOWERED while the screen was open) and customers.takenActiveNumbers(), then calls assertChoosableNumber. CustomerNotFound for an unknown id; CustomerArchived for a household that has left the register — archived records are read-only, they hold no slot and they receive no cards. A BLOCKED HOUSEHOLD IS MOVED LIKE ANY OTHER: a block pauses them at the counter and does not freeze their record, the same division changeGroup and issueCard already make
ONE clock read for the whole act, as issueCard does: the card's issuedAt and both audit entries are the same event

The card is derived HERE, not in the adapter: index from nextCardIndex(await cards.highestIndexForNumber(newNumber)) — THE NEW SLOT'S RUN, not the household's card index — countsAtIssue from composition(members, now) and groupAtIssue from customer.group, so the new card prints TODAY'S counts and TODAY'S group

New port method CustomerRepository.changeCustomerNumber(id: number, customerNumber: number, card: NewCard): Promise<IssuedCard>, documented as ONE TRANSACTION: the number moves and the card is inserted together or neither happens. The precedent is create(), which writes the customer, the household, the certificate and the first card as one. Two writes would have a window in which a household holds 23 and carries 5k4, with nothing in the system able to notice

PrismaCustomerRepository implements it in ONE $transaction: update Customer.customerNumber, then insert the card reading the slot off the JUST-UPDATED row exactly as PrismaCardRepository.issue does, so Card.customerNumber is the NEW number and no caller can pass a different one

A lost race is the DATABASE'S answer: the partial unique index on Customer refuses a number an active household took first and is translated to CustomerNumberTaken(number); an index taken on the slot meanwhile is translated to CardNumberTaken(slot, index) by the same collision reading issue() already does. Both roll the transaction back WHOLE — nothing written

TWO audit entries, because two things happened and each is read on its own: { what: 'customer.numberChanged', changedFields: ['customerNumber'], when, why: 'customerNumber=5→23' } — the numbers ride in why as the one machine-written value ports.ts already documents (a logged reminder writes 'reminderCount=2' there for the same reason) — and the card's own 'customer.card.issued' with why: 'CUSTOMER_NUMBER_CHANGED', written exactly as issueCard writes it. NO REASON IS COLLECTED FROM STAFF (ADR-006)
It returns the IssuedCard the store wrote, so the caller's receipt names the number the register actually holds rather than one the screen worked out
EVERY hand-written fake CustomerRepository in the application tests gains changeCustomerNumber in the same commit, or the suite does not compile

userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to change a household's number where I change its group, and be told exactly which card I am about to print before anything happens. Source: tasks/prd-us-30-change-customer-number.md §US-30.7
acceptanceCriteria: A new Section „Kundennummer“ on /kunden/[id], DIRECTLY AFTER „Gruppe“ — its own section with its own save, presented the way the group control is, because it is the same kind of act: an administrative decision about the register taken for DF's sake. It is DELIBERATELY NOT in the danger zone with the reissue, the block and the archive — those are irreversible things done TO a household — but it borrows the danger zone's CONFIRMATION. It is the ONLY place a number can be changed: the customer list, the counter and the card view offer nothing

NumberControl (client component, src/app/kunden/[id]/number-control.tsx) rendering a <select> of view.numberChoices ascending, opened on the household's current number — the SAME KIND OF CONTROL the registration form uses for the same choice (US-24), so staff meet one control for one decision

After a successful save the control comes back opened on the NEW number, with the vacated one now among the choices
An ARCHIVED household sees the number as a read-only Field, like the group — no control at all

Saving is TWO STEPS, the way a reissue after a loss is: the first button reveals a confirmation naming the chosen number AND the card number that will be issued on it (from numberChoices, NEVER worked out in the component), and only the second button writes. It can only be shown once a number has been chosen, and the card in the household's hand becoming invalid is named in it

A hint under the control states the three consequences, none of which is visible on this screen: the old number is free immediately, the card the household carries becomes invalid, and a new card is printed now. Plus „Noch N freie Nummern“ in the wording de.customers.assignment.freeNumberCount already uses
When the household's own number is the ONLY choice, the hint says no other number is free. The control is NOT DISABLED — a disabled control tells a staff member nothing about why
changeCustomerNumberAction in src/app/kunden/[id]/actions.ts: Zod-validate, call EXACTLY ONE use case, revalidatePath, return state. Business logic here is a bug

A dedicated state type (number-change-state.ts, OUTSIDE the 'use server' module for the reason reissue-state.ts documents) carrying, on success, the old number, the new number and the new card number — the receipt names all three, and after the write the row it was read from is gone

On a refusal the state carries FRESH numberChoices from listNumberChoices, in the patch shape freshPoolAfterRace uses, so the staff member's obvious next move is not a number that provably cannot be saved. Other refusals leave the list alone. After a refusal the staff member STAYS ON THE SCREEN and is told in ONE SHORT SENTENCE what happened

German ONLY in src/i18n/de.ts: heading, hint, the no-other-number hint, both button labels, the pending label, the confirmation sentence naming both numbers and the card, the success receipt and one short sentence per refusal (taken, out of range, unchanged, archived). userStories.title: The record stops saying a number cannot be changed (documentation + ADR)
userStories.description: As the next developer, I need the written record to describe the system that exists, because four documents currently state the opposite in as many words. Source: tasks/prd-us-30-change-customer-number.md §US-30.9
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-016 'a customer number may be changed, and a card keeps the number it was printed with', recorded with the record-adr skill INCLUDING its row in the chapter 9 decision log. CONTEXT: DF's testing — a returning family, a block of numbers kept together, a number typed in wrongly; the reasons are theirs and not the software's. DECISION: the move and the new card are ONE TRANSACTION, every card keeps its own slot, no number history is built. CONSEQUENCES, honestly: Card.customerNumber becomes a SNAPSHOT and is READ AS THE CARD'S NUMBER, which ADR-007 ruled out; the vacated slot's run is what keeps its numbers from being printed twice; the card history reveals past numbers as a side effect and is LEFT CORRECT RATHER THAN OBSCURED

ADR-007: the Card.customerNumber row of the derive-don't-store table is REWRITTEN — it is a key AND a snapshot, and it IS read as the card's number. It links to ADR-016. ADR-007 is AMENDED, NOT SUPERSEDED: the principle holds, one entry in its table changed
ADR-008 gains a sentence: a number changes hands between households AND between numbers for one household, which STRENGTHENS rather than weakens 'a slot, not an identity'

Root CLAUDE.md, the derive-don't-store exception list: the Card.customerNumber paragraph currently ends 'it snapshots NOTHING: a customer number is fixed at registration and released only by archiving … and never read as the card's number'. Rewritten to what is now true, with the pointer to ADR-016
prisma/schema.prisma, the Card.customerNumber doc comment: the same correction — 'as it will always stand' is no longer the case. THE COLUMN ITSELF IS UNCHANGED and prisma/migrations/ is NOT touched
